stages.name: No war fleet of its own
stages.desc: Coasts served by others' fleets, or river craft only

stages.name: Penteconters
stages.desc: Fifty-oared galleys with one bank of rowers

stages.name: Biremes
stages.desc: Two-banked galleys with rams, as on the Assyrian reliefs

stages.name: First triremes on record
stages.desc: Three-banked ships recorded, but fleets still mixed

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Greek and Phoenician kingdoms, among them Kition and Salamis, with penteconters
Luli of Sidon takes refuge on the island and dies there
Amasis of Egypt conquers Cyprus; its kingdoms serve a fleet that already has triremes
The Cypriot kings join Persia and sail with Cambyses against Egypt
The island rises with the Ionians; their fleet wins at sea but Cyprus is reconquered
Cyprus sends one hundred and fifty triremes with Xerxes

states.name: Israel
timeline: Judah, Philistia and the ports of Akko and Achzib; the coast is served by Sidon's fleet
Sennacherib takes Akko and Achzib from Luli and besieges Lachish
Necho II defeats King Josiah of Judah at Megiddo
Babylon destroys Jerusalem; the coast remains without a fleet of its own
Under Persia, the coastal towns are later granted to Sidon and Tyre

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre and Sidon, the leading Phoenician cities, sail two-banked war galleys with rams
Luli, king of Sidon, flees Tyre for Cyprus as Sennacherib takes the coast
Esarhaddon of Assyria destroys Sidon; Tyre's fleet survives offshore
Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon begins a thirteen-year siege of island Tyre
Phoenician triremes form the core of the Persian navy that carries Cambyses to Egypt
Sidon, Tyre and their neighbours send three hundred triremes with Xerxes; Sidon's are the best

states.name: Syria
timeline: The island city of Arwad keeps a Phoenician fleet of two-banked galleys
Abdi-li'ti of Arwad submits to Sennacherib with tribute
Arwad's ships join the Phoenician trireme squadrons of the Persian king
Merbalus of Arwad commands his city's triremes in Xerxes' fleet

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Ionian and Aeolian cities such as Miletus and Phocaea sail penteconters
Persia conquers Ionia; the Phocaeans flee west in their penteconters
Ionian and Aeolian ships, triremes among them, sail with Cambyses
The Ionian Revolt: the cities man trireme fleets against Persia
Defeat at Lade; Miletus is sacked
Ionians, Carians and Cilicians man triremes in Xerxes' fleet

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage, a colony of Tyre, with fifty-oared galleys
Carthaginian and Etruscan ships fight the Phocaeans at Alalia
Tyre's sailors refuse to attack Carthage for Persia
Carthage sends a great fleet of warships with Hamilcar to Sicily

states.name: Greece
timeline: Corinth builds the first Greek triremes; Ameinocles makes four ships for Samos
Corinth and Corcyra fight the oldest Greek sea battle Thucydides knew
Polycrates of Samos rules the Aegean with a hundred penteconters
Polycrates sends forty triremes to serve Cambyses
Laurion silver pays for Themistocles' two hundred Athenian triremes
Some three hundred and seventy Greek triremes fight at Salamis

states.name: Italy
timeline: Greek colonies such as Syracuse and the Etruscan cities sail penteconters
Etruscan ships fight beside Carthage at Alalia
Gelon takes Syracuse; the Sicilian tyrants now keep many triremes
Gelon defeats Carthage at Himera

states.name: Egypt
timeline: The Kushite pharaohs rule; Nile craft, no seagoing war fleet
Psamtik I founds the Saite dynasty with Greek and Carian mercenaries
Necho II builds triremes on the Mediterranean and on the Red Sea
Apries fights a sea battle against the king of Tyre
Persia conquers Egypt; its shipyards build triremes for the Persian king
Two hundred Egyptian triremes sail with Xerxes and fight well at Artemisium

events.title: Ameinocles of Corinth
events.text: Thucydides says this Corinthian shipwright built four ships for Samos about three hundred years before 404 BC.

events.title: Four ships for Samos
events.text: Samos receives the Corinthian-built ships, by Thucydides' account the first Greek triremes.

events.title: Luli flees Tyre
events.text: Luli, king of Sidon, escapes by sea from Tyre to Cyprus as Sennacherib advances.

events.title: Sidon submits
events.text: Sennacherib takes Sidon and puts Ethbaal on its throne in Luli's place.

events.title: Arwad pays tribute
events.text: The king of the island city of Arwad submits to Assyria.

events.title: Siege of Lachish
events.text: Sennacherib storms Lachish in Judah, a siege carved in the same palace as Luli's flight.

events.title: The Nineveh reliefs
events.text: Sennacherib's South-West Palace shows Phoenician galleys with two banks of oars and rams.

events.title: Sennacherib's fleet
events.text: Phoenician shipwrights build ships in Assyria that sail down the rivers to attack Elam.

events.title: Sidon destroyed
events.text: Esarhaddon razes Sidon after its revolt and beheads its king.

events.title: First Greek sea battle
events.text: Corinth fights its colony Corcyra, the oldest Greek naval battle Thucydides knew.

events.title: Psamtik I
events.text: The Saite pharaoh reunites Egypt with Greek and Carian mercenaries.

events.title: Naukratis
events.text: Greek traders settle at Naukratis in the Nile delta.

events.title: Battle of Megiddo
events.text: Necho II defeats and kills King Josiah of Judah on his march north.

events.title: Necho's triremes
events.text: Herodotus writes that Necho built triremes on the Mediterranean.

events.title: Red Sea triremes
events.text: A second squadron of Necho's triremes is built on the Red Sea.

events.title: Necho's canal
events.text: Necho begins a canal from the Nile to the Red Sea but abandons it.

events.title: Around Africa
events.text: Phoenician crews sent by Necho are said to sail right around Africa in three years.

events.title: Massalia founded
events.text: Phocaean colonists found Massalia on the coast of Gaul.

events.title: Siege of Tyre
events.text: Nebuchadnezzar begins a thirteen-year siege of the island city.

events.title: Jerusalem falls
events.text: Babylon destroys Jerusalem and its temple.

events.title: Apries at sea
events.text: Pharaoh Apries sends an army against Sidon and fights the king of Tyre at sea.

events.title: Amasis takes Cyprus
events.text: Herodotus calls Amasis the first ruler to conquer Cyprus.

events.title: Phocaeans flee
events.text: Besieged by the Persians, the Phocaeans sail west with their families in penteconters.

events.title: Hipponax names it
events.text: The poet Hipponax of Ephesus gives the earliest Greek mention of a trireme in verse.

events.title: Battle of Alalia
events.text: Sixty Phocaean penteconters fight one hundred and twenty Carthaginian and Etruscan ships off Corsica.

events.title: Cyrus takes Babylon
events.text: Phoenicia passes to the Persian empire.

events.title: Polycrates of Samos
events.text: The tyrant of Samos dominates the Aegean with a hundred penteconters.

events.title: Cambyses invades Egypt
events.text: Phoenician and Cypriot ships support the Persian conquest of Egypt at Pelusium.

events.title: Forty Samian triremes
events.text: Polycrates sends forty triremes to serve Cambyses.

events.title: Carthage spared
events.text: The Phoenicians refuse to sail against Carthage, their own colony.

events.title: Ionian Revolt
events.text: Miletus leads the Greek cities of Ionia in revolt against Persia.

events.title: Battle off Cyprus
events.text: The Ionian fleet beats the Phoenicians at sea, but Persia wins on land.

events.title: Battle of Lade
events.text: Three hundred and fifty-three Greek triremes lose to six hundred Persian ships.

events.title: Marathon
events.text: A Persian fleet lands an army at Marathon, where the Athenians defeat it.

events.title: Ships from Corinth
events.text: Athens buys twenty ships from Corinth for its war with Aegina.

events.title: Laurion silver
events.text: A rich strike of silver pays for Themistocles' fleet of two hundred triremes.

events.title: Athos canal
events.text: Persia cuts a canal through the Athos peninsula, with Phoenicians the best diggers.

events.title: Gelon's offer
events.text: Gelon of Syracuse offers the Greeks two hundred triremes if he may command.

events.title: Rowing race at Abydos
events.text: Xerxes reviews his fleet at the Hellespont; the Sidonians win the race.

events.title: Artemisium
events.text: The Greek and Persian fleets fight for three days off Euboea.

events.title: Salamis
events.text: In the narrow strait the Greek triremes break Xerxes' fleet.

events.title: Himera
events.text: Gelon and Theron destroy the army of Carthage in Sicily.

chartNote: Share of the area of nine present-day countries, by the most advanced warship each land's own fleets are known to have used. Regions are today's boundaries; the large areas of Egypt and Turkey swing the shares. The evidence is thin and the ancient dates approximate, and whether the trireme was first Greek, Phoenician or Egyptian is still debated: the map is a simplification.
